algorithm: Input: tool (string), input (JSON object), cwd (absolute path, no trailing slash; it stands for the repo root).
command := input.command when tool == 'Bash' and it is a string.
quiet: in command, replace every match of (\s)2>(&1|/dev/null)(\s|$) with $1$3, repeated until nothing changes.
rawSegments := quiet command split on '&&', '||' and on each of the characters ; | & ( ) ` { } and newline; each trimmed; empty ones dropped. A rawSegment is never changed further.

shellWords(s) := s split on whitespace, every " ' and \ removed from each word, empty words dropped. assignment := a word matching ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=\S*$. basename(w) := the text after the last '/' of w, or w when that is empty.

candidates(rawSegment): a work list starts with shellWords(rawSegment); at most 64 distinct word lists are taken from it, first in, first out. For each list L: drop leading assignments; if L is empty go on; replace L[0] by basename(L[0]); add the words joined by one space to the candidates. Then add to the work list every suffix of L (L[k..] for every k ≥ s) for each cut s: s = 1 when L[0] is in prefixWords; s = 2 when L[0] + ' ' + L[1] is in prefixPairs; s = i+1 when L[0] is in shells and L[i] (i ≥ 1) matches ^-[A-Za-z]*c$; s = i+1 when L[0] == 'find' and L[i] is -exec, -execdir, -ok or -okdir.

primary(rawSegment) := shellWords(rawSegment) with leading assignments dropped; then, while the first word is in prefixWords (or the first two words joined by a space are in prefixPairs) and another word follows, those words dropped and then every following word that starts with '-' or is an assignment; then basename of the first word; joined by one space.

segments := every candidate of every rawSegment, plus every primary. pathCandidates(Bash) := for every segment, every word and every part of a word split on '=' and ':'. pathCandidates(other tools) := the string values of input fields named in pathFields.
redirectTargets(rawSegment) := for every match of >[>|]?\s*([^\s<>]+) in it, group 1 with every " ' and \ removed.

normalize(p) := p with '.' and empty parts dropped and each '..' popping one part (a '..' above '/' stays '/'), as an absolute path. resolve(f, p) := p when p starts with '~' (trailing '/' removed; '~' alone stays '~'); normalize(p) when p is absolute; normalize(f + '/' + p) when p is relative. underRoot(a) := a equals cwd or starts with cwd + '/'.

folders: rawSegments are walked in order with a folder set F that starts as {cwd}; each rawSegment (and every candidate, primary, path and redirectTarget taken from it) is judged with the F in force when it is reached. After a rawSegment whose primary starts with cd, pushd, chdir or popd: target := the first later word that does not start with '-' or is exactly '-'. If the word is popd, there is no target, the target is '-', starts with '~' or contains '$', add 'unknown' to F. Otherwise, for every f in F: 'unknown' stays; else a := resolve(f, target), add a if underRoot(a), else add 'unknown'. F only grows (a cd may fail, or the line may stop before it).

inside(p) (with the rawSegment's F) := false if p starts with '~' or contains '$'; underRoot(normalize(p)) when p is absolute; for a relative p: false if 'unknown' is in F, else true iff underRoot(resolve(f, p)) for every f in F. Tools other than Bash judge with F = {cwd}.

base: tool in readTools → read; tool in writeTools → local_write if every pathCandidate is inside(), else unsure (no path → unsure); tool == 'Bash' → unsure if command is missing or empty, read if the primary of every rawSegment is a reader, else local_write; any other tool → unsure, unless a rule with on == 'tool' or on == 'input' matches it (then read, and the rules decide).

reader(segment) := its first word is in readers.commands, or it is 'git' with the second word in readers.git, or it is 'gh' with a second word matching ^[a-z-]+$ and the third word in readers.gh. A word starting with --output or --pre makes it not a reader.

rule matching: on 'tool' → pattern tested on the tool name. on 'command' → pattern tested on the quiet command with every '&&' and '||' removed (Bash only). on 'segment' → tested on each segment; on 'rawSegment' → on each rawSegment (Bash only). on 'path' → tested on each pathCandidate (every tool); when the rule has tools, only for a tool name tools matches. on 'input' → only when tools matches the tool name; pattern tested on canonicalJson(input). on 'outside' → Bash only: a segment matching pattern whose words after the first include a word w such that w or a part of w split on '=' is non-empty, does not start with '-' and is not inside() (so --manifest-path=/x counts /x). on 'redirect' → Bash only: a redirectTarget that does not start with '&', matches pattern and is not inside(). on 'searchRoot' → Bash: for a segment matching pattern, roots := '.' plus every word after its first that does not start with '-' (a search pattern word too); other tools, only when tools matches the tool name: roots := '.' plus the string values of the input fields named in pathFields, with F = {cwd}. It matches when for some root r and some f in F: r contains '$', or f is 'unknown' and r is relative, or resolve(f, r) (f = cwd when r is absolute or starts with '~') matches target. on 'assignment' → Bash only: tested on each leading assignment of each rawSegment, found by walking shellWords(rawSegment) from the start: an assignment is taken; a word in prefixWords (or two words forming a pair in prefixPairs) is skipped, and after it the words starting with '-' are skipped and assignments taken; the walk stops at any other word. A rule with unless does not match a text that unless matches (for 'outside' and 'searchRoot': the segment; for 'redirect': the target; for 'assignment': the assignment word).
tier := the highest rank among base and every matching rule.

channels := over T = {base} ∪ {tier of every matching rule}, with read left out of T unless T is only read: terminalApprove and voiceApprove are true only if they are true for every tier in T; needsOwnerProof is true if it is true for any tier in T. So an outward rule that matched still needs owner proof (and is not terminal-approvable) when an unsure rule ranks the call higher.
Same table and code on every client and in the service; the service keeps max(client tier, its own tier) and ORs/ANDs the channels the same way.

input.command: cd src && cd .. && cd .. && rm -rf x
